payload.headline: Profitability fell while revenue grew; cash generation improved, but the cause of the cash gain is unconfirmed
payload.analysis: Revenue rose from 84 to 96, up about 14.3 percent. Gross profit fell from 36 to 33, and operating expenses rose from 24 to 27, so operating profit dropped from 12 to 6. Gross margin fell from about 42.9 percent to 34.4 percent, and operating margin fell from about 14.3 percent to 6.3 percent. Operating cash flow improved from 6 to 11, an increase of about 83 percent. Capital expenditure rose from 4 to 5, so free cash flow, calculated as operating cash flow minus capital expenditure, rose from 2 to 6. That improvement establishes that the company generated more cash from operations, but it does not establish that earnings improved or that the gain is sustainable, because operating profit fell and the memo gives no cash-flow reconciliation or collection figures. The memo's claim that stronger collection proves sustainable earnings is unsupported; the cash gain could reflect faster collections, delayed supplier payments, lower working capital, or timing.
next_questions: Get the cash-flow reconciliation and working-capital detail (receivables, days sales outstanding, payables, inventory) for years A and B to test whether the higher cash flow came from collections, supplier payment timing, or working-capital changes.
Get the gross-margin drivers (price, volume, product mix, input costs) for year B to explain why revenue growth coincided with falling gross and operating profit.

answer:
The HTTP 200 and the continuing blank lines show the server accepted the request and is holding the connection open as documented. They are not evidence of a server fault. DeepSeek's [Rate Limit & Isolation](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/rate_limit/) page says a non-streaming request may continuously receive empty lines while it waits, and these lines do not affect parsing of the JSON body. A concurrency rejection appears as HTTP 429, so the 200 rules out that status-level failure. The blank lines are not a partial answer, and they do not show whether inference started.

The 75-second stop is a client deadline, not a DeepSeek timeout. HTTPX has connect, read, write, and pool timeouts, with a default of 5 seconds of network inactivity ([Timeouts - HTTPX](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/timeouts/)). Each received blank line resets the read timer. Because lines kept arriving, a 5-second read timeout would not have fired. So the stop points to a separate wall-clock deadline, or to a much larger or disabled read timeout after data stopped. DeepSeek documents only that it closes the connection after 10 minutes if inference has not started. It promises no total-generation time. The failure could be queueing or a slow start, slow generation, or a deadline too short for a legitimate long answer. These observations alone do not separate those causes.

For an appropriate deadline, start with a total client timeout of a few minutes for normal responses, and raise it for prompts expected to produce long answers. Treat it as client policy, not as a guarantee from the 10-minute server rule. Keep the HTTPX read timeout just above the observed gap between blank lines. Timestamped telemetry would distinguish the remaining causes: time to headers, arrival time and content of each blank line and byte, time to first real JSON byte, completion time, status and request ID, model, user_id, in-flight concurrency at request time, and which side closed the connection. Steady blank lines with no body and a server close near 10 minutes mean inference never started. A late but real JSON body means slow generation. A gap longer than the read timeout means a keep-alive or network interruption. Retries returning HTTP 429 point to concurrency limits, not latency.

answer:
The HTTP 200 plus continuing blank lines matches DeepSeek's documented keep-alive behavior for non-streaming requests, not a server error. The [Rate Limit & Isolation](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/rate_limit/) page says such requests may continuously return empty lines while waiting, and those lines do not affect parsing of the JSON body. A request rejected for exceeding concurrency would instead return HTTP 429. So the 200 shows the request was admitted within the concurrency limit at admission time. It does not show that inference has started or that the account was otherwise idle. The blank-line pattern is the main reason to attribute the connection to DeepSeek. But a proxy or gateway returning 200 and buffering could produce a similar shape, and these observations do not fully exclude that.

The 75-second stop is a separate client-owned wall-clock deadline, not a DeepSeek timeout. DeepSeek says the server closes the connection after 10 minutes only if inference has not started. So at 75 seconds the server's own cutoff had not been reached. HTTPX's default is 5 seconds of network inactivity, and its read timeout measures how long to wait for the next chunk of data ([Timeouts - HTTPX](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/timeouts/)). If this client uses HTTPX, each received blank line is still a chunk at the socket level. So it resets the read timer, and a ReadTimeout would not fire while lines continue. Because the observed 75 seconds matches neither the 5-second inactivity default nor the 10-minute server rule, the stop likely came from a custom total-request deadline. Possible failure causes remain queueing or a slow start, slow body generation, a client deadline too short for a legitimate long answer, or an intermediate that stalls.

For diagnosis, set the client deadline longer than 10 minutes if you need to observe the documented server close. A 75-second deadline will always fire first in queueing cases and mask that signal. If you must keep a short deadline for users, add a separate probe with no client deadline so the 10-minute server close remains visible. The most useful telemetry is the timestamp and gap between every blank line, the time from request to the first real JSON byte compared with total time to completion, and who closed the connection and whether blank lines continued until the close. Steady blank lines ending in a server close near 10 minutes mean inference never started. A late but real JSON body means a slow start or slow generation. A gap longer than the configured read timeout means a stalled socket or proxy. Repeated 429 responses mean concurrency limits, not latency.
